interest: Japanese oil and fishing in Borneo suspected as naval reconnaissance.
overview: This State Department file (decimal file 894.20256G) contains intelligence and consular reports from 1931 and 1932 documenting Japanese economic and maritime activities in Borneo, with particular focus on Dutch anxieties regarding Japanese commercial penetration serving as a pretext for naval reconnaissance and espionage. The primary document is a September 30, 1931 voluntary confidential report prepared by American Vice-Consul William K. Ailshie and approved by Consul General Kenneth S. Patton in Batavia, detailing the apprehension of a Japanese vessel taking hydrographic soundings several miles up the Sankoelirang River near Japanese oil concessions in Dutch Borneo, as well as recurring incursions and pillaging by Japanese fishing smacks in Dutch territorial waters. The report is accompanied by a sketch map locating the Japanese oil concessions in eastern Borneo relative to the wider Malay and East Indian archipelago, and is supplemented by a July 15, 1932 cross-reference sheet indexing a despatch from American Consul General Lester Maynard in Singapore regarding Japanese activities off the coast of North Borneo.
